README.md.content:
# Expansion Ideas and Next Steps

Choose a next networking specialization from a measured baseline.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Choose a specialization from a measured baseline

VPN and tunneling add an encapsulated path, so a useful next question is which
traffic selects it and how the inner and outer paths differ. BGP exchanges
reachability and policy between routing peers; one host's static route lookup
provides a foundation rather than a BGP-session observation. Wireless study
adds radio, access-point and authentication considerations to the familiar
address/route/service path. Cloud study adds provider routing and policy
boundaries around the host-level evidence.

Choose one learning goal and draw the extra boundary it would introduce.
For example, "Which destinations would use a tunnel?" needs an existing
working ordinary path, then separate tunnel/interface/route and inner/outer
observations in an approved later lab. This archive establishes the baseline
and plans that next measurement.

**Worked baseline:** baseline has matching A/AAAA answers, successful route
lookups and the intended application response through both families. The
listening control fails from the declared client. Set its readiness to
ready_for_conceptual_extension. The captured topology has no VPN tunnel or
BGP session measurement, so vpnTunnel and bgpPolicy remain not_established.

**Worked prerequisite failure:** route-gap still answers DNS and serves the
application over IPv6, while its IPv4 route-get fails. 198.18.32.0/31 contains
.0 and .1, leaving server .2 outside the prefix. Set readiness to
repair_baseline_first and firstBoundary to ipv4_route. Correct that baseline
before using an advanced extension to explain its symptoms.

**Worked responding failure:** wrong-upstream has a route and HTTP 200, but
the body identifies owned-denial-control rather than the intended application.
Its firstBoundary is application_identity and readiness is
repair_baseline_first. Compare the baseline and choose one next-topic question
with the additional evidence it would require.

Conceptual reading: [IPsec architecture](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4301),
[BGP-4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4271) and
[NIST WLAN guidance](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/153/final).

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

Choose a new output path for each attempt. The capstone creates an outer private
network/mount context and its own client/router/server namespaces, collects the
results and removes its workers and namespaces. Retain receipt.json, inside.json
and capture.pcap. The receipt compares the calling host's routes, links and rules
before and after. A missing tool or refused namespace is a prerequisite issue.

From the exported archive role folder, inspect that new inside.json:

    python3 main.py --inspect /absolute/path/to/fresh-observation/inside.json

This summarizes a supplied file and reports no new network execution. The
assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the
fresh comparison and its provenance in the notebook. Repeat with the alternate
capstone option described in its guide, or with a separately copied learner
case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

## Finish and review

An independent review writes the prediction before checking the reference.
A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

# Expansion Ideas and Next Steps notebook

## Bounded question and next learning goal

TODO: State the question and selected next topic.

## Evidence ladder

Record observation IDs and the exact command/result fields used for each answer. Explain the difference between a listening socket, a selected route, an HTTP response and the intended application.

## Comparison and next measurement

Keep the baseline, changed case, alternative explanation and next command separate. State address family, originating namespace, endpoint and timing. The source captures are historical; fresh collection is required for a live-system conclusion.

## Cleanup and scope

The supplied-record route performs local file analysis. For an owned capstone rerun, retain receipt.json and the worker/namespace cleanup records. An accepted factual assessment leaves explanation and notebook review to the learner or instructor.

"""Expansion Ideas and Next Steps: supplied network-evidence assessment."""
import sys

from archive_lab import main

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main("expansion-plan"))

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

solution/network-notes.md.content:
# Expansion Ideas and Next Steps worked notebook

## Choose a specialization from a measured baseline

VPN and tunneling add an encapsulated path, so a useful next question is which
traffic selects it and how the inner and outer paths differ. BGP exchanges
reachability and policy between routing peers; one host's static route lookup
provides a foundation rather than a BGP-session observation. Wireless study
adds radio, access-point and authentication considerations to the familiar
address/route/service path. Cloud study adds provider routing and policy
boundaries around the host-level evidence.

Choose one learning goal and draw the extra boundary it would introduce.
For example, "Which destinations would use a tunnel?" needs an existing
working ordinary path, then separate tunnel/interface/route and inner/outer
observations in an approved later lab. This archive establishes the baseline
and plans that next measurement.

**Worked baseline:** baseline has matching A/AAAA answers, successful route
lookups and the intended application response through both families. The
listening control fails from the declared client. Set its readiness to
ready_for_conceptual_extension. The captured topology has no VPN tunnel or
BGP session measurement, so vpnTunnel and bgpPolicy remain not_established.

**Worked prerequisite failure:** route-gap still answers DNS and serves the
application over IPv6, while its IPv4 route-get fails. 198.18.32.0/31 contains
.0 and .1, leaving server .2 outside the prefix. Set readiness to
repair_baseline_first and firstBoundary to ipv4_route. Correct that baseline
before using an advanced extension to explain its symptoms.

**Worked responding failure:** wrong-upstream has a route and HTTP 200, but
the body identifies owned-denial-control rather than the intended application.
Its firstBoundary is application_identity and readiness is
repair_baseline_first. Compare the baseline and choose one next-topic question
with the additional evidence it would require.

Conceptual reading: [IPsec architecture](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4301),
[BGP-4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4271) and
[NIST WLAN guidance](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/153/final).


## Evidence locations and conclusion

The record IDs above name complete captured command/result objects in observations.json. Read original argv, family, exit code and response identity together. Preserve the actual .2 destination when comparing the /31 route. The baseline and changed records are different historical attempts with different run markers; compare each body with its own marker.

## Next measurement and scope

Choose the proposed follow-up named above and state the originating node, endpoint, family and expected observation. The supplied record answers remain bounded to their named clients and time. No VPN, BGP, wireless, cloud or public-ingress execution is inferred from this assessment. A live rerun retains its capstone receipt, original failure and cleanup evidence.

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

README.md.content:
# Next Steps Transfer Practice

Transfer the evidence ladder to a route gap and a wrong responding application.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Transfer the diagnostic ladder

Carry one baseline through DNS, the selected family route, the intended
endpoint and application identity, then the exposure control. A successful
earlier step supplies context for the next one. Keep each address family
separate when the results disagree.

**Worked route gap:** baseline.firstBoundary is none. In route-gap, the A
answer is matching_answer, route4 is failed, application6 is
intended_application and firstBoundary is ipv4_route. The exact next lookup
is the recorded equivalent of ip -n ncap-client -4 route get 198.18.32.2.
Read the failed lookup beside the configured /31 and the server .2 address.
A valid lookup for the adjacent router .1 would answer a different question.

**Worked identity gap:** wrong-upstream.route4 is selected, so replacing the
working route does not address this observation. Its application4 is
wrong_application: curl exits zero and HTTP returns 200, yet the response body
names the control application. firstBoundary is application_identity.
Compare the configured upstream 8088 with the reference 9000 and preserve the
original response before changing it.

Write two next-measurement plans, one for each failure. Include source namespace,
destination, protocol/port, expected result and the observation that would
change the conclusion. Explain why a generic "network down" diagnosis loses
the useful difference between these two records.

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

Choose a new output path for each attempt. The capstone creates an outer private
network/mount context and its own client/router/server namespaces, collects the
results and removes its workers and namespaces. Retain receipt.json, inside.json
and capture.pcap. The receipt compares the calling host's routes, links and rules
before and after. A missing tool or refused namespace is a prerequisite issue.

From the exported archive role folder, inspect that new inside.json:

    python3 main.py --inspect /absolute/path/to/fresh-observation/inside.json

This summarizes a supplied file and reports no new network execution. The
assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the
fresh comparison and its provenance in the notebook. Repeat with the alternate
capstone option described in its guide, or with a separately copied learner
case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

## Finish and review

An independent review writes the prediction before checking the reference.
A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

# Next Steps Transfer Practice worked notebook

## Transfer the diagnostic ladder

Carry one baseline through DNS, the selected family route, the intended
endpoint and application identity, then the exposure control. A successful
earlier step supplies context for the next one. Keep each address family
separate when the results disagree.

**Worked route gap:** baseline.firstBoundary is none. In route-gap, the A
answer is matching_answer, route4 is failed, application6 is
intended_application and firstBoundary is ipv4_route. The exact next lookup
is the recorded equivalent of ip -n ncap-client -4 route get 198.18.32.2.
Read the failed lookup beside the configured /31 and the server .2 address.
A valid lookup for the adjacent router .1 would answer a different question.

**Worked identity gap:** wrong-upstream.route4 is selected, so replacing the
working route does not address this observation. Its application4 is
wrong_application: curl exits zero and HTTP returns 200, yet the response body
names the control application. firstBoundary is application_identity.
Compare the configured upstream 8088 with the reference 9000 and preserve the
original response before changing it.

Write two next-measurement plans, one for each failure. Include source namespace,
destination, protocol/port, expected result and the observation that would
change the conclusion. Explain why a generic "network down" diagnosis loses
the useful difference between these two records.


## Evidence locations and conclusion

The record IDs above name complete captured command/result objects in observations.json. Read original argv, family, exit code and response identity together. Preserve the actual .2 destination when comparing the /31 route. The baseline and changed records are different historical attempts with different run markers; compare each body with its own marker.

## Next measurement and scope

Choose the proposed follow-up named above and state the originating node, endpoint, family and expected observation. The supplied record answers remain bounded to their named clients and time. No VPN, BGP, wireless, cloud or public-ingress execution is inferred from this assessment. A live rerun retains its capstone receipt, original failure and cleanup evidence.

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

README.md.content:
# Next Steps Extension Practice

Separate supported local observations from advanced VPN, BGP, wireless and cloud claims.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Audit the scope of an advanced networking claim

A working private application path supports a local reachability conclusion.
Advanced claims need the measurements belonging to that additional boundary.

**Worked local claim:** baseline.application4 and application6 are
intended_application. That supports the recorded client's two private paths.
vpnTunnel, bgpPolicy, wirelessSecurity and cloudSecurityGroup are
not_established: the supplied measurements concern a wired namespace topology,
its static routes and host filtering. They include no tunnel exchange, BGP
peer/announcement, radio authentication or provider security-group observation.

**Worked counterexample:** open-control.control4 and control6 are
control_response. The recorded client now reaches the deliberately admitted
control at 8088. otherClients and internetExposure remain not_established.
One successful source does not establish the behavior of every source or a
path through a public edge.

Choose two claims: one supported by a specific command/result and one requiring
a new measurement. For the latter, draw the extra component and identify the
evidence it would produce in an approved later lab. A tunnel comparison can
identify inner/outer traffic and route selection; a BGP comparison needs a
routing-peer/announcement view; wireless needs radio/authentication evidence;
cloud policy needs its provider-side boundary and a measured request path.

Conceptual reading: [IPsec architecture](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4301),
[BGP-4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4271) and
[NIST WLAN guidance](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/153/final).

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the

case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

# Next Steps Extension Practice worked notebook

## Audit the scope of an advanced networking claim

A working private application path supports a local reachability conclusion.
Advanced claims need the measurements belonging to that additional boundary.

**Worked local claim:** baseline.application4 and application6 are
intended_application. That supports the recorded client's two private paths.
vpnTunnel, bgpPolicy, wirelessSecurity and cloudSecurityGroup are
not_established: the supplied measurements concern a wired namespace topology,
its static routes and host filtering. They include no tunnel exchange, BGP
peer/announcement, radio authentication or provider security-group observation.

**Worked counterexample:** open-control.control4 and control6 are
control_response. The recorded client now reaches the deliberately admitted
control at 8088. otherClients and internetExposure remain not_established.
One successful source does not establish the behavior of every source or a

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

README.md.content:
# Service Exposure Studio

Explain the complete path from client through proxy to the intended loopback application.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Trace the service boundary

Draw client -> router -> server proxy -> loopback backend. Add each observed
address, family and port to that diagram. A reverse proxy can admit a front
request while the application itself remains bound to loopback.

**Worked intended path:** baseline.application4 and application6 are
intended_application. The client requests the recorded server's front port,
and the body identifies owned-operations-capstone with the matching run marker
and /health path. The server listener snapshot makes backendBind4 loopback.
internetExposure remains not_established because the observed client is inside
the owned private topology.

**Worked wrong responder:** wrong-upstream returns 200 through the front port
in both families, but the body names owned-denial-control. Both application
answers are wrong_application and firstBoundary is application_identity.
The faulty upstream is 8088; the intended application is at 127.0.0.1:9000.
A working transport and responding front proxy can therefore coexist with the
wrong application result.

Annotate the diagram with one observation supporting each edge. State what
additional external witness and edge-policy observations a public-exposure
claim would require. The separate extension challenge on this saved attempt
adds a before/after prediction for the wrong-upstream correction; preserve the
original record and compare its body with the baseline.

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

Choose a new output path for each attempt. The capstone creates an outer private
network/mount context and its own client/router/server namespaces, collects the
results and removes its workers and namespaces. Retain receipt.json, inside.json
and capture.pcap. The receipt compares the calling host's routes, links and rules
before and after. A missing tool or refused namespace is a prerequisite issue.

From the exported archive role folder, inspect that new inside.json:

    python3 main.py --inspect /absolute/path/to/fresh-observation/inside.json

This summarizes a supplied file and reports no new network execution. The
assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the
fresh comparison and its provenance in the notebook. Repeat with the alternate
capstone option described in its guide, or with a separately copied learner
case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

## Finish and review

An independent review writes the prediction before checking the reference.
A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

# Service Exposure Studio worked notebook

## Trace the service boundary

Draw client -> router -> server proxy -> loopback backend. Add each observed
address, family and port to that diagram. A reverse proxy can admit a front
request while the application itself remains bound to loopback.

**Worked intended path:** baseline.application4 and application6 are
intended_application. The client requests the recorded server's front port,
and the body identifies owned-operations-capstone with the matching run marker
and /health path. The server listener snapshot makes backendBind4 loopback.
internetExposure remains not_established because the observed client is inside
the owned private topology.

**Worked wrong responder:** wrong-upstream returns 200 through the front port
in both families, but the body names owned-denial-control. Both application
answers are wrong_application and firstBoundary is application_identity.
The faulty upstream is 8088; the intended application is at 127.0.0.1:9000.
A working transport and responding front proxy can therefore coexist with the
wrong application result.

Annotate the diagram with one observation supporting each edge. State what
additional external witness and edge-policy observations a public-exposure
claim would require. The separate extension challenge on this saved attempt
adds a before/after prediction for the wrong-upstream correction; preserve the
original record and compare its body with the baseline.


## Evidence locations and conclusion

The record IDs above name complete captured command/result objects in observations.json. Read original argv, family, exit code and response identity together. Preserve the actual .2 destination when comparing the /31 route. The baseline and changed records are different historical attempts with different run markers; compare each body with its own marker.

## Next measurement and scope

Choose the proposed follow-up named above and state the originating node, endpoint, family and expected observation. The supplied record answers remain bounded to their named clients and time. No VPN, BGP, wireless, cloud or public-ingress execution is inferred from this assessment. A live rerun retains its capstone receipt, original failure and cleanup evidence.

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

README.md.content:
# Service Exposure Transfer Practice

Distinguish address-family evidence, binding snapshots and actual peer requests.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Keep binding and probe families distinct

A server's local socket snapshot and a client's request answer different
questions. Record both the originating namespace and the destination family
before combining them.

**Worked binding:** baseline.backendBind4 is loopback. backendBind6 is
not_listed in the supplied socket snapshot. This states what that snapshot
shows; a new or different listener requires a fresh observation. The actual
directUpstream command targets the external IPv6 server address on port 9000,
so directBackend.family is the number 6 and its result is request_failed.

That one IPv6 failure is not an IPv4 client test of the IPv4 loopback backend,
and it does not isolate a firewall cause by itself. To investigate a live
version, compare a server-local IPv4 loopback request, an owned IPv4 peer
request, the actual binding and the corresponding policy. Preserve each
origin/family rather than collapsing them into "port open" or "port closed."

**Worked transfer:** alternate changes the front port to 8087 and name to
amber.capstone.test. Its two application answers remain intended_application;
backendBind4 remains loopback and directBackend.family remains 6.
Inspect the command arguments instead of assuming the default port or name.

**Worked mixed result:** route-gap.application4 is request_failed,
application6 is intended_application and firstBoundary is ipv4_route.
Use the failed IPv4 lookup and excluded .2 address to explain the difference.
An IPv6 success supplies an IPv6 result.

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

Choose a new output path for each attempt. The capstone creates an outer private
network/mount context and its own client/router/server namespaces, collects the
results and removes its workers and namespaces. Retain receipt.json, inside.json
and capture.pcap. The receipt compares the calling host's routes, links and rules
before and after. A missing tool or refused namespace is a prerequisite issue.

From the exported archive role folder, inspect that new inside.json:

    python3 main.py --inspect /absolute/path/to/fresh-observation/inside.json

This summarizes a supplied file and reports no new network execution. The
assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the
fresh comparison and its provenance in the notebook. Repeat with the alternate
capstone option described in its guide, or with a separately copied learner
case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

## Finish and review

An independent review writes the prediction before checking the reference.
A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

solution/network-notes.md.content:
# Service Exposure Transfer Practice worked notebook

## Keep binding and probe families distinct

A server's local socket snapshot and a client's request answer different
questions. Record both the originating namespace and the destination family
before combining them.

**Worked binding:** baseline.backendBind4 is loopback. backendBind6 is
not_listed in the supplied socket snapshot. This states what that snapshot
shows; a new or different listener requires a fresh observation. The actual
directUpstream command targets the external IPv6 server address on port 9000,
so directBackend.family is the number 6 and its result is request_failed.

That one IPv6 failure is not an IPv4 client test of the IPv4 loopback backend,
and it does not isolate a firewall cause by itself. To investigate a live
version, compare a server-local IPv4 loopback request, an owned IPv4 peer
request, the actual binding and the corresponding policy. Preserve each
origin/family rather than collapsing them into "port open" or "port closed."

**Worked transfer:** alternate changes the front port to 8087 and name to
amber.capstone.test. Its two application answers remain intended_application;
backendBind4 remains loopback and directBackend.family remains 6.
Inspect the command arguments instead of assuming the default port or name.

**Worked mixed result:** route-gap.application4 is request_failed,
application6 is intended_application and firstBoundary is ipv4_route.
Use the failed IPv4 lookup and excluded .2 address to explain the difference.
An IPv6 success supplies an IPv6 result.


## Evidence locations and conclusion

The record IDs above name complete captured command/result objects in observations.json. Read original argv, family, exit code and response identity together. Preserve the actual .2 destination when comparing the /31 route. The baseline and changed records are different historical attempts with different run markers; compare each body with its own marker.

## Next measurement and scope

Choose the proposed follow-up named above and state the originating node, endpoint, family and expected observation. The supplied record answers remain bounded to their named clients and time. No VPN, BGP, wireless, cloud or public-ingress execution is inferred from this assessment. A live rerun retains its capstone receipt, original failure and cleanup evidence.

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

README.md.content:
# Service Exposure Extension Practice

Compare a protected control with the same control after a narrow policy change.

## Prepare and run

This optional archive follows the required addressing, route, listener, diagnostic
and exposure units. Its supplied-record route uses five actual isolated Linux
captures. Python 3.10 or later is the supplied checking tool; the networking task
is to interpret observations, complete an assessment and explain the evidence.
Use the same cases independently or pause with an instructor at each evidence
boundary.

Open the starter in the site IDE, retain the reference as a separate attempt,
and keep the imported files together. Save assessment.json and network-notes.md,
reopen the same assignment to confirm those edits, then export the complete ZIP.
From the exported project folder, run the selected role:

    cd starter
    python3 main.py

The reference uses the parallel solution folder. Exit 1 means an assessment is
incomplete or disagrees with the observations; exit 2 means an input file is
invalid; exit 0 means the factual fields agree. The report always leaves
reasoning and notebook review open. Local analysis creates no network resources.
Complete the null answer fields using the vocabulary and worked comparisons
below. Explanations belong in network-notes.md; keep the documented answer keys.

## Input inventory and topology

- main.py selects this exercise; archive_lab.py reads and checks the data.
- observations.json contains the exact recorded inside.json text, original
  command arguments, outputs, exit codes, timestamps and capture provenance.
- assessment.json is the editable factual assessment. network-notes.md records
  the question, predictions, cited fields, explanation and next measurement.
- edge-cases.md supplies further comparisons. SOURCES.md identifies each
  original capture and its hash.

The client is 198.18.31.2 and 2001:db8:31::2. A router connects it to the server
at 198.18.32.2 and 2001:db8:32::2. The default name is blue.capstone.test. The
resolver listens at server port 15353; the front proxy listens at TCP 8080; the
intended application binds IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1:9000. An owned control listens
at TCP 8088. The default policy admits the declared client's proxy and resolver
traffic and denies its control traffic. The alternate capture changes the name
to amber.capstone.test and the proxy port to 8087.

Read these fields in each record's raw object:

| Field | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| dns.A / dns.AAAA | Actual lookup command and returned family-specific answer |
| routeGet4 / routeGet6 | Route selected for that family's server address |
| listeners | Server-namespace socket snapshot, including address and port |
| policy4 / policy6 | The recorded family-specific filtering rules |
| http4 / http6 | Client request arguments, curl exit, HTTP status and response body |
| denied4 / denied6 | Client requests to the listening control on port 8088 |
| directUpstream | One client request to the external IPv6 address on port 9000 |
| case | The configured IPv4 service prefix and proxy upstream port |

Display a readable observation field directly from either role folder:

    python3 main.py --show route-gap --field routeGet4
    python3 main.py --show wrong-upstream --field http4
    python3 main.py --show baseline --field listeners
    python3 main.py --show open-control --field policy4

Omit --field to show that entire named record. This decodes the preserved raw
text without requiring a separate JSON editor or Python code.

The top-level completed flag is the older lab's overall verdict. Derive this
exercise's answers from the observations instead. A record describes one
originating namespace, endpoint, family and time; further claims need further
measurements. The original run markers are ephemeral response identifiers from
an already closed isolated lab.

## Record set

| Record | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | Working dual-stack application path; control requests fail |
| alternate | Working path using a different name and front proxy port |
| route-gap | A /31 service route excludes server .2; IPv6 still works |
| wrong-upstream | Front proxy reaches the control application at upstream 8088 |
| open-control | The same control becomes reachable after an admission-rule change |

A 200 response establishes an HTTP response, then the requested endpoint,
application identity, run marker and path identify what answered. A listening
socket alone establishes the local binding snapshot. A failed request alone
does not identify a firewall cause: inspect the route, actual listener and
matching policy as separate evidence.

## Compare a measured policy change

Read the baseline and open-control listener, route and rule snapshots before
using the request outcomes as a before/after comparison. Both captures retain
a real control listener at 8088 and a working application through the proxy.

**Worked baseline:** control4 and control6 are request_failed, while
application4 is intended_application. The captured rules admit the declared
client's front-proxy traffic and leave new control traffic outside that
admission. Read the recorded timeout beside the viable route and listener.

**Worked changed boundary:** open-control adds admission for that client's
8088 traffic. control4 and control6 become control_response; application4
stays intended_application. The response identifies the control application,
which is the intended responder for the separate 8088 probe. The same control
identity behind a request for the front application would be a different result.

otherClients and internetExposure remain not_established. The pair supports
the changed rule and observed client in this private topology; it has no
measurement of another client or a public ingress path. Record the exact
family-specific admission rules, retain the baseline as the rollback
comparison, and identify the next source/path measurement needed for a wider
claim. The analysis route changes no rules; live work uses the capstone's
owned isolated context and retains its cleanup receipt.

## Collect a fresh owned-lab comparison

The complete [capstone source and guide](https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems/tree/f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812/NS-03-network-systems-lab-17) provide the optional live
Linux route. Use an owned disposable Linux VM with root privileges and network
and mount namespaces. On an administered Debian/Ubuntu practice VM, install
the tools once:

    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install python3 git iproute2 iptables util-linux curl dnsutils tcpdump dnsmasq-base

Check out the pinned source in a new working directory:

    git clone https://github.com/instruction-material/Network-Systems.git network-practice
    cd network-practice
    git checkout f37b558cfe75c7e6348a4689e1c06284da1f2812
    cd NS-03-network-systems-lab-17/solution
    sudo python3 main.py --output ./fresh-observation

Choose a new output path for each attempt. The capstone creates an outer private
network/mount context and its own client/router/server namespaces, collects the
results and removes its workers and namespaces. Retain receipt.json, inside.json
and capture.pcap. The receipt compares the calling host's routes, links and rules
before and after. A missing tool or refused namespace is a prerequisite issue.

From the exported archive role folder, inspect that new inside.json:

    python3 main.py --inspect /absolute/path/to/fresh-observation/inside.json

This summarizes a supplied file and reports no new network execution. The
assessment route continues to refer to its five named source records; put the
fresh comparison and its provenance in the notebook. Repeat with the alternate
capstone option described in its guide, or with a separately copied learner
case.json using /31 versus /30 or upstream 8088 versus 9000. Preserve the
failed observation before correcting that one field. The open-control source
record comes from the capstone verifier's controlled rule regression; its exact
rule and request output are already supplied here.

## Finish and review

An independent review writes the prediction before checking the reference.
A guided review pauses after the topology, the first conflicting observation,
the bounded conclusion and the next measurement. Cite record IDs and exact
command/result fields in the notebook. Explain one alternative cause and the
evidence that would distinguish it. Reopen/export the saved role and rerun its
command. The green factual report confirms the assessed fields; explanation,
topology and scope notes remain part of review.

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.

# Service Exposure Extension Practice worked notebook

## Compare a measured policy change

Read the baseline and open-control listener, route and rule snapshots before
using the request outcomes as a before/after comparison. Both captures retain
a real control listener at 8088 and a working application through the proxy.

**Worked baseline:** control4 and control6 are request_failed, while
application4 is intended_application. The captured rules admit the declared
client's front-proxy traffic and leave new control traffic outside that
admission. Read the recorded timeout beside the viable route and listener.

**Worked changed boundary:** open-control adds admission for that client's
8088 traffic. control4 and control6 become control_response; application4
stays intended_application. The response identifies the control application,
which is the intended responder for the separate 8088 probe. The same control
identity behind a request for the front application would be a different result.

otherClients and internetExposure remain not_established. The pair supports
the changed rule and observed client in this private topology; it has no
measurement of another client or a public ingress path. Record the exact
family-specific admission rules, retain the baseline as the rollback
comparison, and identify the next source/path measurement needed for a wider
claim. The analysis route changes no rules; live work uses the capstone's
owned isolated context and retains its cleanup receipt.


## Evidence locations and conclusion

The record IDs above name complete captured command/result objects in observations.json. Read original argv, family, exit code and response identity together. Preserve the actual .2 destination when comparing the /31 route. The baseline and changed records are different historical attempts with different run markers; compare each body with its own marker.

## Next measurement and scope

Choose the proposed follow-up named above and state the originating node, endpoint, family and expected observation. The supplied record answers remain bounded to their named clients and time. No VPN, BGP, wireless, cloud or public-ingress execution is inferred from this assessment. A live rerun retains its capstone receipt, original failure and cleanup evidence.

solution/edge-cases.md.content:
# Further checks

- An A answer or an IPv6 success alone leaves the IPv4 application path unverified.
- HTTP 200 needs the requested endpoint, expected application identity, matching run marker and path.
- A failed request to a port without an observed listener cannot isolate a policy effect.
- An IPv4 loopback listener and one IPv6 client probe measure different boundaries.
- A successful recorded client says nothing about unmeasured clients, the public internet or an advanced protocol.
- Missing observations remain unknown. Compare the alternate recorded port and name without assuming the default values.
